title: Dogfood the orchestrator on its own downstream work
body: Plan 2026-05-09-003 just closed; the orchestrator now has the substrate to consume its own state-projection output. Rather than hand-code plans 010 + 004, drive them through supervisor.dispatch_volley and treat every terminal-non-success as signal for orchestrator improvement. Convention follows the harness_frictions_v1/v2 pattern from memory: real volleys surface real frictions; clustered findings get promoted to v3 fixes plan. Parent meta-plan structure follows nested-orchestration v1 (plan 2026-05-02-003): children declare orchestration block pointing up to this parent; parent is a regular plan that gets pointed at. spawn_reason: operator_manual on both children (operator deliberately authored both as downstream work after plan 003 closed).

Treating it as infra avoids the Goal Governance V1 objective_contract document requirement at lock time. Same framing as plan 010 (printing-press-adapter skill) and plan 003 (state-projection v0).

title: FINDING (interpretive-disagreement, then RESOLVED): F002 original framing was based on wrong cause attribution
body: Hand-coding F002 surfaced that the prompt template is already small (~5KB). The original D007 hypothesis was 'implementer prompt template loads too much context' — but inventory found the template loads only plan_id + feature dict + steps + forbidden/required CLI lists. The 4.92M iter0 input_tokens came from elsewhere. Cost driver: ClaudeCLIExecutor.dispatch() aggregates `input_tokens + cache_read_input_tokens + cache_creation_input_tokens` into a single `tokens_in` field. Cache_read accumulates across every agent tool-use turn — pytest output, file reads, etc. all get cache_read'd into context on every subsequent turn. Original D007 100:1 ratio was a measurement-attribution mistake: 'input tokens' was really 'sum of all input + cached-read sums across all turns of an autonomous agent loop'. The prompt template was never the issue. CLASSIFICATION: interpretive-disagreement (we built the wrong mental model of where cost comes from). RESOLUTION: F002 reshipped with the actual safe levers (see D016).

title: F002 (cost-lever ship) closed: --exclude-dynamic-system-prompt-sections + TEST_DISCIPLINE_NOTE
body: Shipped two safe levers (both OAuth-compatible): (a) ClaudeCLIExecutor.dispatch() argv now includes `--exclude-dynamic-system-prompt-sections` on every dispatch — moves cwd/env/git/memory paths from cached system prompt to first user message, improving cross-dispatch cache reuse. (b) prompts.py exports TEST_DISCIPLINE_NOTE constant, threaded into both iter0 and iterN implementer prompt paths — instructs agent to prefer targeted tests over full sweeps with explicit rationale about cache_read accumulation. Tests: 11 new fixture tests in test_v3_f002_cost_levers.py pin both levers + 10KB prompt-size invariant; test_f005b_executor_argv updated for new flag position. Full orchestrate sweep 1828 passed / 7 skipped. REJECTED ALTERNATIVES: --bare flag (would disable OAuth auth → break operator's subscription-based dispatch). --max-budget-usd (different concern; future v4 candidate). Re-measurement of actual token savings deferred to a real dispatch (e.g. v3 F003 or plan 010 F002 dispatched after this lands).

title: F004 token cost: 7.09M tokens / 139:1 ratio — partial regression vs F003
body: v3 F004 total: 7.09M in / 50.9K out / 139:1 ratio. v3 F001 baseline: 8.86M/140:1. v3 F003 post-F002 levers: 4.42M/98:1. F004 came in at ~1.6x F003 cost. Plausible drivers: F004 had a 2-iteration volley with auditor flagging real findings (more iterations = more accumulated cache_read), iter1 implementer alone consumed 4.08M which is double the F003 iter0 baseline (2.39M). Hypothesis: when the implementer is responding to substantive defects (not just iter0 fresh start), tool-use turns multiply because the agent re-reads code + audit envelope + makes incremental fixes. F002 levers still help vs pre-fix baseline but the iter1 working-against-findings path is more expensive than iter0 fresh start. Future v4 candidate: trim auditor envelope re-reads on iterN.

title: v3.1 hot-fix: validate_prod_gates enum-vs-string coercion (SpinDine cross-repo dogfood)
body: Operator hit a real validator bug from a SpinDine v2 dispatch attempt — `validate_prod_gates` typed `human_gates` as `list[str]` but `plan_loader._load_plan` passes `plan.human_gates` (a `list[HumanGate]` per the Pydantic model). `HumanGate` is a plain Enum (not StrEnum), so `"pre_impl" in {HumanGate.pre_impl}` is always False and every required gate was reported missing. 4 SpinDine dispatch attempts blocked. CLASSIFICATION: feature_defect (same class as v3 F004 i1 findings — bug caught by cross-repo dogfood). FIX: defensive coerce on the validator side — `gates = {(g.value if hasattr(g, 'value') else g) for g in (human_gates or [])}`. Single-line set-comprehension; both str and Enum shapes round-trip correctly. 10 new fixture tests in test_validate_prod_gates_enum_coercion.py pin every case: enum members satisfy required, mixed str+enum, required_override path also coerces, no-regression on string-only inputs. Full sweep 1871 passed / 7 skipped. PATTERN: this is v3-class friction surfaced via cross-repo dogfood (SpinDine), exactly the mechanism v3 was designed to capture. v3.1 hot-fix shape (single commit + regression test + ledger entry); no separate plan needed because scope is one-line bugfix. SpinDine session can rebase and re-dispatch.

title: FINDING (interpretive_disagreement): codex auditor verdict=blocked on advisory-only finding terminated supervisor prematurely
body: Plan 010 F002 dispatch: codex auditor returned audit_status=blocked because its read-only sandbox couldn't run pytest. Single finding was severity=advisory, category=test_coverage — non-substantive per the F003 taxonomy (would classify as `environmental_reproduction_failure` if it were a real finding). But the supervisor terminated `blocked after 1 round` because the AUDITOR VERDICT STRING was 'blocked' — not because the FINDINGS warranted termination. Mismatch: a single advisory finding should not block, but the auditor's pre-emptive 'blocked' verdict string did. v3 F003 ENVIRONMENTAL_BLOCKER short-circuit fires on a *finding* with that class, not on the verdict string itself. CLASSIFICATION: interpretive_disagreement between the auditor's terminal verdict and the substantive content of its findings. Single occurrence so far — not a v4 cluster trigger. Watch for repeats. Candidate fix would be supervisor reconciling: if auditor verdict=blocked but ALL findings are advisory-only, treat as paused_on_gate (or even signed_off-with-environmental-note), not blocked-terminal. Capture for future v4 frictions plan if pattern repeats.

title: OBSERVATION: lock-time scope-change protocol prevented paid mid-dispatch failure
body: Plan 004 was status:draft with two internal inconsistencies that would have blocked or wasted the F001 dispatch: (a) child_charter.allowed_paths still pointed at archived axiom/packages/** dirs (predates D006 rename); (b) F001 acceptance #4 required <firebase-project-id> smoke but parent_acceptance_item deferred credentials. The pre-dispatch review caught both, rescope shipped at d43bd08 with D007 rationale, then dispatch ran clean. PATTERN: lock-time inspection (cross-check child_charter vs feature steps + dependencies declared deferred) is cheap; mid-dispatch discovery of the same gaps would have cost ~9M tokens to learn. Worth adding as a doctor preflight check in a future v4: 'compare allowed_paths against feature step paths' + 'flag acceptance items that name resources listed as deferred elsewhere in the plan'. Capture for future v4 frictions cluster.
